correctness.rationale: If K has an imaginary-axis eigenvector, taking the real part of its eigenvector identity shows that the sum of strictly positive site losses on it is zero, so it is a Hamiltonian eigenvector vanishing on all sinks. Conversely all such Hamiltonian modes form a reducing subspace for K, evolving unitarily; its orthogonal complement is exponentially damped in finite dimension. The complement is the sum of the sink-visible spectral projection ranges, equivalently the Krylov space. Independently constructed H₁=J−MᵀM+I using the 5×10 point-versus-pair incidence M and MMᵀ=3I+J, yielding eigenspace dimensions 1,4,5 for 3,−2,1. The symmetric off-diagonal update has rank two, leaving at least three 1-eigenvectors; two site evaluations cannot see them all. A rank-two resolvent calculation reproduces the entire stated characteristic polynomial. Exact weighted walks and determinant expansion reproduce −2(t−1)^3 for (1,2,8) in the specified order and −2 for (0,1,2,4,5) at t=1. The triple's projected ranks at t=1 are 1,3,3, so exactly 7/10 is captured from I/10, versus 1 for nonunit t by the nonzero minor. At t=1 the 1-eigenspace demands five sinks. Fixed finite-time evolution is continuous by the matrix exponential; no uniform decay-rate assertion is used.
residual_risks: Conclusions assume adjacency hopping, strictly positive constant site losses and one-excitation finite-dimensional dynamics. They do not classify degree-normalized, diffusion or Laplacian detectors, or finite-time performance.

value.rationale: A natural resource question is how many local sinks guarantee trapping of an arbitrary single-particle state. A lone defective edge sharply reduces that number, but an invariant eigenspace still forbids using two sinks. The same exact triple for all positive nonunit weights and its jump from 7/10 capture at symmetry to full capture separate eventual capture from finite-time behavior; this is not just a perturbed example at a single weight or a generic-rank computation.
residual_risks: No quantitative uniform time scale or experimental efficiency prediction is asserted.
